Weekly China recap. Huge week as onshore sell-off intensifies: - Offshore China was flattish MXCN -0.3%, onshore CSI300 falls again -2.9%, now down for the 12th straight week, longest in history (previous was 9 weeks), total drawdown -18%. Star50 $KSTR and ChiNext $CNXT also continue to sell off hard, -13.7% / -10.1% respectively for the week - US FCC has voted to stop recognizing all electronics test labs in China from Dec 2028. Chinese labs tested 82% of devices seeking FCC approval in 2025 and US labs under 4%, Chair Brendan Carr says. Some notable products affected: smartphones, routers/wi-fi networking, IoT / cameras / smart-home, PCs / tablets / consumer computing, Wearables, Drones, and more - Chinese news outlet Jiemian News (界面新闻) reports that Apple $AAPL relaxed some of its yield-related quality-control standards due to limited production capacity for the iPhone Duo. This reportedly increased the likelihood of units prone to display failures reaching the market - Major Chinese Cloud Service Providers (CSPS) including Alibaba $BABA, Tencent $TCEHY, & Bytedance, have requested long-term supply agreements (LTAs) for server memory from Samsung & SK Hynix $SKHY beyond the typical 3~5 year term. Some customers are seeking ultra-long-term contracts securing memory supplies for 10 years through 2035. Requested LTAs cover DDR5 and LPDDR5 - PBoC established the Bond Market NBFI Swap Facility to provide liquidity support to eligible institutions facing large-scale redemptions under systemic bond-market stress on Oct 26 https://www.news.cn/fortune/20261026/043399a6396548b4b32ee433c79e3f3b/c.html - China completed the deployment of 800B Yuan (~$120B USD) under its new policy-based financial instruments on Oct 28 https://www1.xinhuanet.com/20261028/ca09d57a56b94728bb96458d0a8804c0/c.html - NFRA issued new asset-management trust rules, tightening requirements around risk management, sales and investments https://www.nfra.gov.cn/cn/view/pages/ItemDetail.html?docId=1277211&itemId=915 - Reuters reports that CXMT plans to begin small-scale production of HBM3E within the next 2 months. Current yield of 20%. CXMT's test results showed that its HBM3E performance was closer to SK Hynix's pervious generation HBM3 and falls short of SK Hynix's HBM3E - Rumor that all Chinese open source model releases going forward (beginning with Kimi K3.1 Pro) will have cybersecurity capabilities stripped before release. Chinese open source releases on the horizon are GLM 5.5 and Qwen 4 - China Sept Industrial Profits/Revenue rose +14.1%/+6.6% yoy, respectively. Seasonally adjusted and in sequential terms, Profits unchanged (vs. +0.6% in Aug) and Revenue -0.1% (vs. +0.9% in Aug) - 3Q'26 EARNINGS: 80% reported, earnings -11% yoy (+10% excluding non-bank Financials)
